humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark uses Czech historical document archives as its textual source, but the evaluated competence is general semantic topic localization and word-level span extraction rather than historical disciplinary knowledge.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: A text-only benchmark that uses OCR-transcribed historical Czech texts paired with natural language topic names and descriptions.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Evaluates text-level topic presence detection (modeled as binary text classification) and word-level topic span localization (modeled as span extraction/information extraction).

general_purpose_benchmark.note: The benchmark is specialized for the specific NLP task of topic localization and span extraction in historical Czech.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates multiple generative models, including GPT-5 (gpt-5-2-2025-12-11, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5-nano), Llama 3 (Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 3.2 3B Instruct), Gemma 3 (27B, 4B), Gemini 3 Pro, and gpt-oss-20b.

quantitative_metrics.note: Uses Precision, Recall, F1 score, and Intersection over Union (IoU) at both text and word levels.

published_after_march_2023.note: The paper was published on arXiv in March 2026.

summary: The paper introduces CzechTopic, a human-annotated benchmark for zero-shot topic localization in historical Czech documents. Models are evaluated on their ability to identify and extract precise word-level spans representing topics defined by a name and description. The evaluation framework is grounded in inter-annotator agreement rather than a single gold reference.
key_findings: The best-performing LLM (GPT-5-2) achieved a word-level F1 of 61.1 and IoU of 48.7, remaining significantly below the human baseline (68.7 F1, 57.2 IoU). A substantial performance gap of 47.9 F1 points exists between the best and worst LLMs. Additionally, specialized BERT-based models fine-tuned on distilled data (such as robeczech with 48.3 word F1) remain highly competitive against larger LLMs.
facets_explanation: The reference annotations were created by multiple annotators whose exact professional or academic backgrounds are not explicitly stated, though they followed detailed guidelines and attended regular alignment meetings. Instead of collapsing annotations into a single consensus key, the benchmark preserves divergent interpretations as signal, evaluating models against each individual annotator's spans and averaging the resulting agreement metrics. The task focuses on matching text spans to topic descriptions provided directly within the prompt, meaning no knowledge beyond the stimulus is required.
results_explanation: The paper reports an answer format gap of 0.104 F1 (10 percentage points) between the 'Matching (x Tagging)' span extraction strategies in Table 3. The human baseline for word-level topic localization is 68.7 F1, while the best model ('gpt-5-2-2025-12-11') achieves 61.1 F1, representing an 8-point gap (7.6 rounded up). Because the dataset is exclusively in Czech, no cross-cultural or multilingual asymmetry is discussed.
